text: In Genesis 6 there is a world corrupt all the way down and one man who "walked with God" (6:9). The narrator does not soften the first of these. Every imagination of the human heart is only evil continually (6:5), the earth is filled with violence (6:11), and Yahweh is sorry he made man (6:6). Noah receives no commission to reform any of this. He is told to build. The chapter gives more words to the ark's specifications (6:14–16) than to the corruption that makes the ark necessary, and the reason is plain: Noah builds to a measure he did not set. The ark exists as dimensions before it exists as wood. Of Noah's own part the narrator says only one thing: "according to all that God commanded him, so did he" (6:22). Noah is named righteous before he does anything (6:9). In this chapter his righteousness becomes visible as obedience, as his willingness to build what God, who has seen the whole world, says will be needed.
